title: P32.14 release search orders every result list alphabetically by label and empty labels sort first: unfiltered browse opens on unlabelled records in every large compartment (osm_physical 3,089 pages before the first named record)
evidence: code: search_index.py:123 _KEYSET_ORDER = 'r.label_sort, r.entity_type, r.entity_id' is the ORDER BY for every query and browse (no bm25/rank anywhere in search()); normalize_sort_key('') returns '' so empty labels sort before any text. recorded-execution: the landed build_search_index + search called unchanged over C3's sha256-verified parquet (osm_physical.parquet sha256 860845d7e093..., public_record.parquet a3d631cff8ab...); docs/build/logs/next-phase/K3/tools/a_order2.py -> docs/build/logs/next-phase/K3/out/a_order2.txt: no-q browse page 1 = 50/50 unlabelled in osm_physical, public_record, operator_accepted, portal, sig_graph; unlabelled records sorted first: osm_physical 154,483/154,705 (3,089 pages of 50), public_record 19,828 (396 pages), operator_accepted 12,881 (257); q='Winnipeg' returns an unlabelled record first; q='Canberra' returns '109 Canberra Ave…' addresses in alphabetical order. The landed HTML says order 'is not a relevance score'. Consequence (inference): once deployed (ACT-17), the 'Complete browse' links and broad queries on /search/ open on UUID-only rows; relevance ranking is absent, not merely weak. Distinct from K0 NEW-1 (label emptiness) and K12b NEW-10 (the live 500-row substring island).

title: On the real release the P32.14 index layout is 488.6 MB (osm_physical 301 MB, mostly text claim-id and facet tables) and the API verifies each file by reading it whole into memory on a 512 MiB service (latent until activation)
evidence: recorded-execution: docs/build/logs/next-phase/K3/tools/a_baseline.py ran the landed build_search_index unchanged over the 12 compartment parquets of release sig-2026-09-27-ce480ab1 (C3 capture) -> docs/build/logs/next-phase/K3/idx/p3214/sizes.json: total 488,562,688 B for 232,625 records; osm_physical 301,428,736; public_record 88,072,192; operator_accepted 50,864,128. dbstat on osm_physical: identifiers 88.8 MB (773,747 rows: entity id + record key + ~3.0 claim ids per record as TEXT), facets 61.2 MB, records 45.4 MB, six covering indexes 68.4 MB + unique key index 12.4 MB, FTS tables 25.2 MB. code: release_search.py:120 'data = path.read_bytes()' then hashlib.sha256(data) — the whole file in memory on first request per (publication, compartment). research/G1-ops.md line 73: sig-api 1 vCPU / 512 Mi, max 2. Inference: the first osm_physical search after activation allocates ~301 MB plus the Python process, and concurrent first requests for other compartments add more — OOM/503 risk; the files are also read over the gcsfuse registry mount (G3 §4.3), latency unmeasured. A compact v2 layout measured 77.0 MB (+~22 MB claim table) for the same corpus (docs/build/logs/next-phase/K3/idx/v2/sizes.json). K0 §2.3's 37.7 MB covered an FTS table only.

title: Exact-token matching does not remove the misleading hits: P32.14 answers 'ICE' with ice stadiums and 'Maryland', 'Georgia', 'Idaho' and 'Oklahoma' with street names in other states and countries
surface: /v1/releases/<pub>/compartments/<c>/search (landed engine, not deployed) over release sig-2026-09-27-ce480ab1
evidence: docs/build/logs/next-phase/K3/tools/a_bench.py -> docs/build/logs/next-phase/K3/out/a_bench.txt (landed si.search over all 12 compartments): 'ICE' -> 'Nottingham Ice Stadium (Lower Parliament St)' (ogl_uk3), 'Dundonald International Ice Bowl' (operator_accepted) — 4 hits; 'Maryland' -> Winnipeg 'Cornish & Maryland', 'Maryland & Sargent', 'Maryland & Wellington' (11 hits, none a place); 'Georgia' -> Vancouver 'Beatty St and W Georgia St' (60); 'Idaho' -> Washington 'I-5 @ MP 119.7: Idaho Ave' (13); 'Oklahoma' -> DC 'Benning Rd and Oklahoma Ave NE' (2); 'Texas' -> 'CAPITAL OF TEXAS HWY' rows. The engine has no place resolution, alias table or case-sensitive acronym handling (search_index.py:517-694). K12b NEW-10 found the same class on the live substring island and expected 'exact-token matching' to fix it; this shows tokens alone are insufficient — the fix is place resolution ahead of text and case-sensitive acronym aliases (design/K3-search.md §4). Wrong-conclusion risk on a sensitive query (J3 journalist 'ICE-linked systems').

title: The technology facet offered by the release search API, its no-JS HTML form and the workspace URL contract is structurally empty (0 facet rows in every compartment), and the kind facet has a single value
evidence: code: release.py:469 builds each search row with 'technology': str(row.get('technology') or '') from shaped sites.jsonl rows; exports/src/exports/shaping.py contains no 'technology' key (grep: 0 hits), and the release parquet has no technology column (21 columns, duckdb describe); _facet_pairs adds a technology facet only when non-empty. recorded-execution: docs/build/logs/next-phase/K3/out/a_order2.txt — technology facet rows = 0 in osm_physical, public_record, operator_accepted, portal, sig_graph (and all 12 in a_baseline); kind facet has exactly 1 value ('deployment'). The API still accepts technology= and the HTML form renders a Technology select (release_pages.py:570). Refines F-325 (published exports carry no technology field) by showing the user-facing search control it disables; a journalist's 'ALPR' filter can never match.

title: Release search makes the reader choose one of 12 licence compartments before searching, and a two-letter code returns 422 in every compartment that lacks it (10 of 12 for 'TX')
evidence: code: search.astro renders one <form> per compartment ('Search this compartment'); the API route is /v1/releases/{pub}/compartments/{c}/search with no cross-compartment variant; the no-JS HTML states search is 'deliberately not federated' (release_pages.py:660). search_index.py short-query branch raises 422 query_too_short unless the 2-letter string is a jurisdiction facet value in that compartment. recorded-execution: docs/build/logs/next-phase/K3/out/a_bench.txt B04 'TX': 100 hits from portal+public_record and 422 query_too_short from the other 10 compartments. Consequence (inference): a reader must run up to 12 searches (the release has 12 compartments; C3 capture) to learn where a name appears, and any client that federates sees errors for valid place codes. Keeping licences separate does not require separate requests: results can be grouped per compartment with licence lines in one response (design/K3-search.md §5.3; federated prototype p50 1.45 ms warm).

title: Live-spine /v1/search cannot find an entity by its own id and returns substring matches in UUID order, so it is no substitute for a public search
evidence: code: _SEARCH_MATCH selects entity_id IN (SELECT entity_id FROM entity_identifier WHERE value ILIKE '%q%') ORDER BY e.entity_id — the entity's own UUID is not an identifier value, and order is UUID (creation) order with no ranking. live-read (K12b, 21:34Z; docs/build/logs/next-phase/K12b/json/api__v1_search_q_01a0a720_9b9a_7890_a8ae_99705e6b5368_limit_5.json): q=<the operator's research-queue agency UUID> -> results []; api__v1_search_q_Austin_limit_10.json: 10 results in entity_id order, 7 of them 'traffic_camera:camreg_austin_tx:austin_tx_traffic_cameras:N' identifier strings. Developers (P7) are told to resolve ids via /id/{type}/{id}, but the 422 hint only fires for short queries. Relevance: K12b F-23 proposes surfacing /v1/search on the site; besides K0 I-10 / G3 REL-05 (live spine is not a public-page source), the route's matching would reproduce the substring and ordering failures.

title: The release publishes no agency, vendor or organization records, so no release-pinned search can answer the journalist's name queries; the 'expose /v1/search' shortcut (K12b F-23) would answer them only from the live spine that K0 I-10 and G3 REL-05 bar from public pages
surface: release sig-2026-09-27-ce480ab1: */sites parquet, sig_graph/sharing_edges.csv, web/network.json (C3 capture)
evidence: duckdb over C3's capture: 232,625 distinct records, entity_type = 'deployment' only; the network agency ids (e.g. 01a0a720-9b9a-7890-a8ae-99705e6b5368, 01a0a720-af12-7946-bfe3-1accab0e34ae 'Austin Police Department' per the live API) and the hub 01a0d751-0901-7a6c-8789-06bab8c7456e ('Vigilant Solutions (LEARN)') are in none of the 12 compartment parquets (0 rows); labels matching 'Vigilant' 0, 'Flock' 0; the only named organization in the release is the partner_ref string 'Vigilant Solutions (LEARN)' on 130 sharing_edges.csv rows. Benchmark (docs/build/logs/next-phase/K3/tools/queries.py): 6 of 40 persona queries (B16-B19 vendors/agencies, B31 the research-queue UUID, and the ICE entity behind B11) have no release record to find. K12b §4 and F-23 suggest exposing the API's /v1/search as a first pass; K0 §4.1 I-10 and G3 §6.4 (REL-05) classify /v1/search as live-spine, 'not a citation', never a public page's data source. Inference: journalist name search depends on K2 publishing agency/vendor/organization entities into the release (and its label rule), not on the search engine; K3's first pass must say so in its empty states. Related to K0 NEW-1 and K12b NEW-1 (names exist in the spine), which concern labels, not release coverage.
